subtype: Approach: working backward from the exam date [Thinking]
passage: Vikas stood in front of the wall calendar and counted: nineteen weeks to the entrance test. On an index card went the syllabus, twenty-four units. Then the subtracting began. The last three weeks would be revision only. Four weeks in the middle would go to full mock papers. That left twelve weeks for twenty-four units, so two units a week, no more, no less. Vikas wrote 2/week in red and pinned the card above the desk. Darshan, who studied at the next desk, leaned over. “And if a week goes wrong?” “Then it eats into the mock weeks, and I move things.” Vikas breathed out. A large, blurry number had become a small list.

qa.q: How many units must Vikas finish each week?
What might Vikas be feeling after the calculation?
qa.a: Relief and steadiness: the big blurry number became a small list 🙂.

qa.q: What else could Vikas add to the plan, and why?
qa.a: A spare week for illness or slow topics, since a buffer keeps one bad week from breaking the whole plan.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Darshan?
qa.a: Darshan, studying at the next desk, sees a vague worry turned into a schedule, and may want a plan like it or worry about one bad week.

grounding: A student counts the weeks before the exam, lists the units and works backward to a weekly number including revision and mocks.
